newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds says Cheyne to be intl banking head.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds says Cheyne to be intl banking head.

text.p: British banking heavyweight Lloyds TSB Group Plc said on Friday that Iain Cheyne would become managing director of International Banking when David Pirrie retires from the role at the end of June.
Cheyne, 54, is currently general manager of corporate and institutional banking and also deputy chairman of share settlement system Crestco.

Cheyne, a solicitor, was awarded a CBE (Commander of the British Empire) in 1994 for his work in leading the financial restructuring of the Canary Wharf development in London's Docklands and negotiating the contract under which the British goverment agreed the construction of the Jubilee Line underground extension.

He was made general manager of corporate banking in 1991 and has "extensive experience gained through work on strategic planning, including the acquisition of Cheltenham & Gloucester Building Society in 1995 and overseas assignments", Lloyds TSB said.

From the end of June control of its holdings in U.S. fund managers Weiss,Peck & Greer and Investment Advisers Inc. would move into the international division from corporate and institutional banking, the bank added.
Pirrie will also resign as an executive director of Lloyds TSB when he retires.
Pirrie spent most of his career with the Lloyds Bank group. He joined the Bank of London and South America as a trainee in 1959, completing his training in Brazil.

Many of his early appointments were in Brazil and he became general manager for the country in 1975. He returned to London in 1981. Before becoming director of international and private banking he was director of UK retail banking.
